disputed: Whether the media companies settled purely to end costly, uncertain litigation (their stated position, and the position of some outside observers who called the underlying lawsuits weak) or specifically to curry favor with the administration (given the timing relative to pending merger/regulatory approvals) is a matter of inference, not documented intent, though the timing itself is a matter of public record. Whether Trump's DOJ will actually pay his personal claims, and in what amount, remains unresolved and unconfirmed.

items: Disney/ABC News settled Trump's defamation suit (over anchor George Stephanopoulos's characterization of the E. Jean Carroll civil verdict) for $15 million to Trump's presidential library plus $1 million in legal fees, in December 2024, before Trump took office. (Marketplace (https://www.marketplace.org/story/2025/08/22/where-is-trumps-award-settlement-money-going))

Paramount (CBS's parent company) settled Trump's lawsuit over a '60 Minutes' interview edit for $16 million to the library on July 2, 2025 - while Trump was president and while Paramount separately needed FCC approval, under newly installed Republican Chairman Brendan Carr, for its sale to Skydance Media. The merger was approved roughly three weeks after the settlement. (NPR (https://www.npr.org/2025/07/02/nx-s1-5454790/cbs-settlement-trump-60-minutes-harris-interview-analysis); MS NOW (https://www.ms.now/opinion/trump-media-tech-settlements-defamation-lawsuits-86-million))

Trump publicly celebrated the CBS payout and suggested he could receive an additional $20 million from Skydance. Meta separately paid $25 million to resolve a suit over Trump's removal from Facebook after January 6 - a case outside lawyers said was weaker for Trump than the ABC case, yet still settled. (Forbes (https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/07/22/trump-celebrates-16-million-60-minutes-settlement-and-suggests-hell-get-another-20-million-too/); NPR (https://www.npr.org/2025/07/02/nx-s1-5454790/cbs-settlement-trump-60-minutes-harris-interview-analysis))

A CBS analysis found Trump's presidential library had received approximately $63 million through settlements with Paramount, ABC, Meta, and X combined by mid-2025; a separate report found he received a collective $59 million from YouTube's and other tech companies' parent companies, and that his 2025 media/tech settlements totaled roughly $86 million. Reporting separately noted a broader $2.2 billion windfall tied to his business interests in 2025. (MS NOW (https://www.ms.now/opinion/trump-media-tech-settlements-defamation-lawsuits-86-million))
sections.label: Media and tech settlements funding Trump's presidential library

items: While out of office in 2023 and 2024, Trump filed two administrative claims (a legal precursor to suing the government) against the DOJ under the Federal Tort Claims Act: one over the 2016 Russia investigation, one over the 2022 Mar-a-Lago classified documents search, together seeking roughly $230 million ($115M+ each, including punitive damages). (PBS (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-says-the-government-owes-him-a-lot-of-money-over-federal-probes-heres-how-he-could-be-paid))

As president, Trump would be the one whose administration decides whether to pay out his own claims - CNN and PBS both noted the conflict of interest, since DOJ officials who would need to approve any settlement previously served as his personal defense attorneys or represented his allies. (CNN (https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/22/politics/trump-doj-request-230-mil-explained))

In October 2025, Trump discussed the matter in the Oval Office alongside AG Pam Bondi and FBI Director Kash Patel, saying: 'I have a lawsuit that was doing very well. And when I became president, I said: I'm sort of suing myself... How do you settle the lawsuit? I'll say: Give me X dollars, right?' He said any payout would go to charity. In a later speech, he inflated the figure to $1 billion, saying 'I hereby give myself $1B.' (Axios (https://www.axios.com/2025/10/21/trump-justice-department-payment-investigations); Yahoo/HuffPost (https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-brags-demanding-own-government-221248950.html))

As of late 2025, there is no public confirmation the claims have been paid; the DOJ is not required to publicly announce settlements of administrative claims of this kind. (CNN (https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/22/politics/trump-doj-request-230-mil-explained))
sections.label: Seeking $230 million+ in damages from his own DOJ
